title: FastAPI job response (mlflow/server/job_api.py:Job): new fields must be added to exact-dict assertions in tests/server/jobs/test_endpoint.py
answers: Why does tests/server/jobs/test_endpoint.py fail after adding a field to the job response?
How does a job submit or cancel response show the creator field?
What do I update when I add a new field to the native FastAPI Job model?
body:
Path: Job submit and cancel responses from the native FastAPI job routes are serialized from mlflow/server/job_api.py:Job via `Job.from_job_entity`, which maps each job entity field into the response model.
Rule: FastAPI serializes optional `None` fields, so a new field such as `creator: str | None = None` appears in the JSON with a null value even for creator-less jobs. The exact-dict assertions in tests/server/jobs/test_endpoint.py:test_job_submit and tests/server/jobs/test_endpoint.py:test_job_cancel must list the new key (for example `"creator": None`), or the tests fail.
Constraints: Keep the field in the wire shape rather than hiding it from the tests; the creator value is what the job search ownership filter reads. Applies to the job response model only, not to the Flask job endpoints.
applies: Changes to the native FastAPI Job response model and its exact-match tests.
says: Show who created the job in the response when submitting or canceling jobs.
The job submission response should include creator information for ownership filtering in job search.
Why does the job cancel response return null for creator when no owner exists?
Include creator attributes in job payloads to allow filtering jobs by their owner.
search: In `mlflow/server/job_api.py:Job.from_job_entity`, new fields added to the native FastAPI `Job` model serialize `None` values (e.g. `creator: str | None = None`) in submit and cancel endpoint responses. Unit tests in `tests/server/jobs/test_endpoint.py:test_job_submit` and `tests/server/jobs/test_endpoint.py:test_job_cancel` must include the new key in exact dictionary assertions rather than omitting it. The creator field must remain in the serialized wire payload because the job search ownership filter depends on it. Guidance applies exclusively to native FastAPI job response models and does not apply to Flask job endpoints.
